name: Antala Industries
summary: Antala Industries makes BOPP bags, BOPP printing and lamination rolls and PP woven bags for food processing, fertiliser, chemical, cement and seed customers from a single plant in Rajkot, Gujarat; it began as the partnership firm Octagon Industries in 2021 and became a company in August 2024. Total income grew from ₹12.6 cr in FY24 to ₹47.5 cr in FY26 and profit rose 133% in FY26 to ₹4.24 cr, with debt to equity low at 0.25. The whole ₹23.33 cr issue is fresh, with ₹10.68 cr for working capital and ₹5.89 cr for new machinery, and promoters keep about 52% after the issue. At the upper band the post-issue P/E on FY26 profit is about 19.2x, below the median of the two listed peers named in the offer document, while the top 10 customers still make up 56% of revenue.

fh1.finding: Total income rose from ₹12.59 cr (FY24) to ₹47.53 cr (FY26), a CAGR of about 94%.

fh2.finding: Total income grew every year: ₹12.59 cr, ₹31.98 cr, ₹47.53 cr (FY24–FY26).

fh3.finding: Debt to equity was 0.25 in FY26 (borrowings ₹4.19 cr vs net worth ₹17.03 cr), and 0.08 at September 2026.

fh4.finding: Borrowings rose from ₹0.36 cr to ₹4.19 cr over FY24–FY26, far faster than the 3.8x rise in total income, though they fell to ₹1.75 cr by September 2026.

fh5.finding: Net worth rose every year: ₹3.54 cr, ₹12.19 cr, ₹17.03 cr (FY24–FY26), and ₹22.17 cr at September 2026.

fh6.finding: Operating cash flow figures were not found in public sources.

pr1.finding: Profit after tax grew about 133% in FY26, to ₹4.24 cr from ₹1.82 cr.

pr2.finding: Net margin moved from 7.1% (FY24) to 5.7% (FY25) and 8.9% (FY26), higher than three years ago.

pr3.finding: Return on net worth was 24.88% in FY26 (ROE stated as 33.26%).

pr5.finding: Peer margins were not found in public sources.

va1.finding: Post-issue P/E of about 19.2x on FY26 profit (₹81.45 cr market cap vs ₹4.24 cr PAT) vs a peer median of 21.6x (Dhaval Packaging 18.5x, Knack Packaging 24.6x).

va2.finding: Post-issue price to book of about 1.8x (₹81.45 cr market cap vs ₹45.5 cr post-issue net worth) vs a peer median of about 6.0x derived from peer EPS, P/E and NAV.

va3.finding: Peer market cap to sales figures were not found in public sources.

va4.finding: No details of pre-IPO share issues or transfers were found in public sources.

pg1.finding: Promoters hold 52.04% after the issue, down from 72.93%.

pg2.finding: No information on pledged promoter shares was found.

pg3.finding: Related-party transaction figures were not found in public sources.

pg4.finding: No information on regulatory action against promoters was found.

is1.finding: The entire ₹23.33 cr issue is fresh; there is no offer for sale.

is2.finding: The issue is about 28.6% of the ₹81.45 cr post-issue market cap.

is3.finding: No selling shareholders, because there is no offer for sale.

up1.finding: ₹5.89 cr, or about 25% of the issue, buys new plant and machinery for the Rajkot facility.

up2.finding: None of the proceeds are earmarked for repaying debt; the named uses are working capital and machinery.

up3.finding: The general corporate purposes amount is not stated; the ₹6.76 cr left after named uses also covers issue expenses.

up4.finding: No proceeds go to repaying any loans, including from promoters or group companies.

lg1.finding: Litigation amounts were not found in public sources.

lg2.finding: No information on criminal or regulatory cases was found.

lg3.finding: Contingent liabilities were not found in public sources.

rk1.finding: The top 10 customers made up 56.43% of revenue in the six months to September 2026, with the largest at 19.61%.

rk2.finding: Supplier concentration figures were not found in public sources.

rk3.finding: The business started as partnership firm Octagon Industries in April 2021, so about 5.5 years of operating history.

rk4.finding: Auditor remarks were not found in public sources.
